title: Crop Insurance Policy Records Held by One Member
content:
**Rule.** Under Crop Insurance a member may hold any number of policy records (no maximum per member), one for each crop and county and crop year; how records of one member combine is set by the association's rule that a member's acreage of one crop in one county for one crop year sits under a single policy record.

There is no cap on how many Crop Insurance policy records one member holds. What sets the count is the member's farming: each distinct combination of crop, county and crop year is its own record.

| Combination held by a member (hypothetical) | Policy records |
|---|---|
| Corn in one county, one crop year | one |
| Corn and soybeans in the same county, one crop year | two, one per crop |
| Corn in two counties, one crop year | two, one per county |
| Corn in one county over three crop years | three, one per crop year |

**Basis Q&A.**

*Does a member who already holds several Crop Insurance policy records reach a limit?* No. The number of records a member may hold has no maximum.

*Does a new crop year of the same crop in the same county count as a separate record?* Yes. A record is held for each crop and county and crop year, so a different crop year is a different record.
